bonus_mechanics: Massachusetts is decoupled from IRC 168(k): Massachusetts depreciation is computed under IRC 168 as if the taxpayer elected not to take the bonus allowance, in the year placed in service and all later years. special_rules: Separate MA depreciation and basis; gain or loss on sale uses MA basis. Same decoupling applies to corporate excise (no difference for entities found).

PA 24 of 2025 (signed 7 Oct 2025; MCL 206.30(1)(ee)): for tax years beginning after 31 Dec 2024, IRC 168(k) applies as in effect on 31 Dec 2024 (pre-OBBBA), so Michigan allows 40% bonus for 2025 property, not the federal 100%. Taxpayer reports an addition equal to the federal depreciation deduction under OBBBA minus the depreciation allowed under pre-OBBBA 168(k) (including regular depreciation). Treasury example: 10,000 asset, federal 100% deduction, Michigan 40% bonus 4,000 plus 600 MACRS = 4,600, addition 5,400.
conformity_date: MCL 206.4 (excerpt): Code in effect on 1 Jan 2025 or, at the taxpayer's option, in effect for the tax year; PA 24 then freezes 163(j), 168(k), 174 and 179 at their 31 Dec 2024 versions

bonus_mechanics: Minn. Stat. 290.0131 subd. 9: 80 percent of the 168(k) depreciation deduction is an addition in the year claimed. 290.0132 subd. 9: in each of the five following taxable years, one-fifth of the 'delayed depreciation' (the addition minus any positive NOL generated that year) is a subtraction. Net: 20% of the federal bonus in year 1, then 16% of it in each of the next five years.
conformity_date: 2018-12-31 (Code as amended through 31 Dec 2018 plus 290.0111 items, per the 2021 and 2022 statute editions); later updated to 1 May 2023 with retroactive federal changes
special_rules: 179: addition under subd. 10 applies only to property placed in service before 1 Jan 2020 (80% of the excess over 179 as of 31 Dec 2003, i.e. the old 25,000/200,000 limits), with one-fifth subtractions for five years under 290.0132 subd. 14, so a 2021 return still carries subtractions for 2016-2019 property. Property placed in service after 31 Dec 2019 takes the federal 179 amount with no addition. Delayed bonus depreciation addition is reduced by NOL generated in the year of addition. Corporations use 290.0133 subd. 11/12 (same 80% rule); S corporation shareholders carry the subtraction.
verify_note: Statute text fetched 2026-10-06 from the 2022 edition (290.0131, 290.0132) and 2021/2022 editions (290.01 subd. 31). Federal 179 amounts are from the federal note (status verify), applied because the 179 addition does not reach property placed in service after 2019. The 20% net is arithmetic on the statute, not a quoted figure.

bonus_mechanics: Mississippi does not allow the federal special depreciation allowance. Federal Form 4562 is completed twice; the second, labelled 'Mississippi', computes depreciation 'without taking into account any special depreciation allowance (generally line 14 of Federal Form 4562)'. The difference is an addition; 'any additional depreciation expense for purposes of this state due to the basis adjustment not being made' is a deduction (2021 corporate booklet, Form 83-122 lines 6 and 13). For an individual the difference goes on Schedule N / Schedule C-1.

special_rules: Separate Mississippi depreciation and basis (full basis, no reduction for the special allowance). 179: booklet says Mississippi follows the TCJA increase from 500,000 to 1,000,000; it does not state the phase-out or whether annual indexing applies (federal indexed 2021 is 1,050,000 / 2,620,000). Aviation property exception under HB 1356.

bonus_mechanics: Income Tax Notice 80-23-003 (20 Oct 2023), HB 1733 (signed 27 Mar 2023, effective 1 Jan 2023): for tax years beginning after 31 Dec 2022, expenditures for qualified property or qualified improvement property are eligible for 100% bonus depreciation and may be deducted in the year placed in service. 'Qualified property' means 168(k) and 'qualified improvement property' means 168(e)(6), each as they existed on 1 Jan 2021. The taxpayer may elect the bonus 'and/or' depreciate under IRC 168; the election is by the return due date including extensions and is irrevocable unless the Commissioner allows a change. The total of all methods cannot exceed 100% of cost. The rate is a state rate, independent of the federal phase-down (federal was 80% for 2023).

Pre-2023 property keeps the old Mississippi basis. Aviation property rule from HB 1356 (2021). 179 figures are the federal amounts for 2023 because the notice says Mississippi follows 179 'in effect for that year'.

bonus_mechanics: Missouri starts from federal AGI (RSMo 143.121.1) and has no add-back for IRC 168(k) bonus on property bought after 30 June 2003. The only 168 modification in 143.121 is for property purchased 1 Jul 2002 to 30 Jun 2003 (30% allowance of the Job Creation and Worker Assistance Act of 2002). So the federal bonus (100% for 2021 property) flows through with no state adjustment and Missouri depreciation equals federal depreciation.
conformity_date: No fixed Code date for ordinary depreciation: 143.121 starts from federal AGI and cites the Code 'as amended'. The only fixed-date reference is the 2002-2003 carve-out (IRC of 1986 as in effect 1 Jan 2002).
special_rules: Residual 2002-2003 rule (143.121.2(3), 143.121.3(7), 143.121.3(9)): add back the excess of the federal 168 deduction over what 168 as in effect 1 Jan 2002 would have allowed, on property purchased 1 Jul 2002-30 Jun 2003; subtract the shortfall in later years; on sale, subtract any addition not yet recovered. Effectively exhausted for personal property (recovery 20 years or less) but a calculator holding such an asset should apply it (my reasoning, not an agency statement). NOL: 143.121.2(4) limits Missouri NOL deductions to a 20-year carryforward and 2-year carryback, with exceptions for 172(b)(1)(G) and 172(i); a loss created by bonus or 179 is therefore tracked separately from the federal NOL (my reading of the statute; Form MO-5090 is the DOR's NOL addition sheet, not read). 163(j): 143.121.2(6) and 3(11) (tax years from 2018) let Missouri subtract interest disallowed under 163(j) in the year disallowed and add it back in the year later deducted federally.
source_citation: RSMo 143.121.1, 2(3), 2(4), 2(6), 3(7), 3(9), 3(11), as reproduced (unamended text) in General Assembly bill HCS HBs 594 & 508, perfected, 1st Regular Session, 103rd G.A. (2025); DOR Form MO-1040 2025 instructions and MO-1120 2025 instructions (search excerpts: only the 2002-2003 property adjustment is described)

Conclusion that 2021 follows federal is therefore from the current text plus absence of any other 168(k) modification. Federal 100% and the 179 figures are from the federal note (status verify). A search-engine summary of dor.mo.gov and a COST/Bloomberg lead agree but are not relied on.

bonus_mechanics: No Missouri action on P.L. 119-21 was found. Because Missouri starts from federal AGI and cites the Code 'as amended', the federal bonus flows through unchanged: 100% for property acquired after 19 Jan 2025, 40% (60% for long-production-period property and certain aircraft) for property acquired before 20 Jan 2025 per the federal note. No add-back. This is an inference from the statute's structure; no Missouri agency statement about 2025 depreciation was read.
conformity_date: Rolling in effect (143.121 starts from federal AGI; Code cited 'as amended'); no Missouri statute found that freezes or decouples any OBBBA depreciation provision.
change_note: No Missouri statutory change on depreciation found. Federal OBBBA depreciation changes reach Missouri taxpayers automatically through federal AGI. HB 594 (2025 session) added a 100% subtraction of capital gains from TY2025 (143.121.3(14), per the perfected bill text; DOR news release excerpt 'First State to Fully Exempt Capital Gains Tax' says effective 1 Jan 2025). DOR 2025 year-changes excerpts say the OBBBA tips, overtime, car-loan-interest and senior deductions are NOT available on the Missouri return; those are below-AGI federal deductions, not depreciation.
special_rules: No Missouri 168(n) modification in 143.121, so the federal qualified production property deduction flows through (decouples_168n false is from the absence of a modification, not an agency statement). 179: no Missouri modification, so federal 2,500,000 / 4,000,000 (P.L. 119-21 s.70306) applies. Open: the capital gain subtraction applies to 'income reported as a capital gain for federal income tax purposes'; recapture of 1245 gain is ordinary income federally and so is not obviously covered, and whether net 1231 gain is covered was not found. Ask DOR before applying it to the sale of depreciated business property. Residual 2002-2003, NOL and 163(j) rules as 2021.
source_citation: RSMo 143.121 as reproduced in HCS HBs 594 & 508 (perfected, 2025 session); DOR 2025 Individual Income Tax Year Changes and 2025 Tax Legislative Changes pages (search excerpts only; both returned 403); DOR news release on HB 594 (search excerpt)
